The sawmill's session-loyalty find table, referenced from the station's Bonus.Lootables. A Roll grants what ELSE a cycle handed over: how MUCH of the thing you made is the action's own Recipe.Yield plus its OutputItems rolls, and a find can only ever ADD something different, never multiply that. Finds arrive as drop-list items, a different thing from the planks those rolls add.

ONE roll, and the held hatchet is felt twice in it: it drives HOW OFTEN a find happens (the Chance, entirely tool-driven up to 90 percent on the best hatchet) and HOW DEEP that find is (the tier Ladder). Time at the bench feeds the same ladder score, so a better hatchet arrives at the deeper tables sooner and a worse one gets there by staying longer. Since each tier pays more offcuts than the one below (one pull at T1 and T2, two at T3), scaling the tier by tool is also what makes a good hatchet shake loose more material - no separate roll needed to say the same thing twice.

THE TOOL SCORE holds the SAME RATIO the Mill action's own plank ladder and ContributionScale use - quality 10, item level 0.1, gather power 1.0 - so one curve ranks every hatchet identically everywhere on the bench and retuning what 'a better tool' means is one decision. Quality dominates, item level breaks ties inside a quality tier, and power rewards the genuinely better cutter; no two of those rank the vanilla ladder alone. On that scale: Wood 10.6, Crude 10.55, Copper 11.3, Iron 22.3, Thorium 33.5, Cobalt 34.0, Adamantite 34.5, Onyxium 40.9, Mithril 45.5, Sawmiller's Hatchet 55.55.

Each use of that score below carries its own multiplier, and the multiplier is the only thing that differs: the Chance uses 1.62x so the trophy lands exactly on the 90 percent cap, and the Ladder uses a QUARTER (2.5 / 0.025 / 0.25) because its score is summed with rpgstations:cycle_count, which runs 10 to about 124 across a session. At full scale the tool alone would put an iron hatchet past the ladder's second floor before the third cycle, erasing the loyalty the ladder exists to reward. Ranking is untouched in both cases; only the magnitude is made fit for its purpose.

Note also that an ItemDropList cannot read factors at all - a drop table is a fixed weighted bag. Every 'better tool gives better loot' effect therefore has to be expressed at the Roll level, which is why the tool rides the Chance and the Ladder rather than anything inside the tables.

Each of this jar's Sawmill lootables holds its own concern so a pack can replace exactly one: this file is the loyalty ladder any worker can reach, SawmillTrophy is the Sawmiller's Hatchet chase, and SawmillMasterworkFinds is the fourth tier that chase pays out.

Rolls.$Comment:
Conditions gate the whole roll on rpgstations:cycle_count 10 or higher, so the first nine cycles of a session never even roll - finds reward staying at the bench, not tapping it - AND on tool quality 2 or better, so a starter Wood, Crude or Copper hatchet mills its planks but never shakes a find loose; iron-grade steel is where finds begin.

Chance then decides HOW OFTEN, and the hatchet drives it entirely: BasePercent is 0, so the whole probability comes from the tool score, capped at 90 percent. The weights are the canonical ratio at 1.62x (16.2 / 0.162 / 1.62), picked so the Sawmiller's Hatchet lands exactly on that cap while the ranking stays identical to every other tool curve on the bench. Across the eligible hatchets: iron about 36 percent, the thorium-to-adamantite band 54 to 56, onyxium 66, mithril 74, and the trophy 90. Finds go from occasional to near-constant purely on the tool you bring, which is the single biggest reason to chase a better one.

The zero base is deliberate rather than an omission: the quality-2 Condition already decides WHO may find at all, so the curve is free to start from nothing and be pure tool. Raising the base lifts every eligible tool together and compresses the spread against the 90 cap, so retune the weights before the base if the spread is what needs changing.

Ladder then decides HOW DEEP, summing the session's cycle count with the quarter-scale tool score and taking the HIGHEST floor reached. Floors are not cumulative, so exactly one table grants. Cycle 10 opens T1, 25 opens T2, and 50 opens T3, with a better hatchet crossing each sooner - an iron worker reaches T2 around cycle 19 and a mithril one around cycle 14, while the trophy is deeper still from its first eligible cycle.

The tables pay offcuts from the shared byproduct list plus their own life essence: T1 offcuts alone, T2 adding essence, T3 doubling the offcuts and making essence near-certain with a small concentrated jackpot. A ten-minute session runs about 124 cycles, so past cycle 50 the top tier covers well over half of them. A floor's own celebration only plays when its table actually paid, so the cue stays silent on a cycle whose table resolved to nothing.
